_note: Pre-registered 2026-11-03 (late), BEFORE any tactical allocation signal was computed or any result existed. Do not edit to fit a result. To change a criterion, add a dated entry to docs/research/log.md saying why, then edit.
idea: Faber-style tactical asset allocation: hold each of five asset classes only while its month-end price is above the average of its last 10 month-end prices, otherwise hold cash. The most common simple systematic approach among retail traders. Reported results: 1972 to 2005 Sharpe 0.81, CAGR 11.7%, max drawdown 9.5%; 2006 to March 2025 out of sample Sharpe 0.68, CAGR 6.05%, max drawdown 11.7% (Concretum Group, a vendor; not checked against the papers). Expectation stated up front: lower drawdown than buy and hold, not more money. See docs/research/what-people-do.md section 2A.
universe_note: Fixed now. Faber used IEF for bonds and GSG for commodities; IBKR serves AGG and DBC with the full history (the NASDAQ-listed names lose older history), so AGG and DBC are used, chosen for data length not performance.

rule.signal: On the last trading day of each month: an asset is 'on' if its close is above the simple average of its last M month-end closes including the current one (M = 10 for the primary).
rule.weights: each 'on' asset gets 20% of equity; assets that are 'off' are replaced by cash (no re-weighting of the others)
rule.fill: next trading day's close, whole shares, sells before buys
rule.cash_return: 0 (conservative: the original uses Treasury bills; IBKR pays interest on idle cash, so this understates the strategy)
rule.costs: tempo.backtest.Costs commission and the SEC fee on sells, plus slippage in bps per side; base 1 bp, sweep 0, 1, 3, 5, 10
rule.prices: IBKR daily bars, ADJUSTED_LAST; today's unfinished bar dropped; sample starts when all five assets have data

benchmarks: equal weight of the same five assets, always held, rebalanced monthly (isolates what the timing rule adds)
60% SPY and 40% AGG, rebalanced monthly (the standard comparison)

variants_tried.note: Only the primary can pass criteria 1 to 7. All four are reported.

negative_control: 200 versions with the same random permutation of days applied to all five assets (keeps each asset's returns and the correlations between assets, destroys serial structure, which a trend filter needs).
pass_all_of: primary net Sharpe at 1 bp per side at or above BOTH the always-held equal-weight benchmark and the 60/40
primary max drawdown shallower than BOTH SPY buy and hold and the always-held equal-weight benchmark
primary net CAGR above the 60/40's net CAGR
primary net Sharpe above 0 in both halves of the sample
t-statistic of the primary's mean daily net return at 1 bp above 3.0 (Harvey, Liu, Zhu)
primary net CAGR above 0 at 5 bps per side
primary beats at least 95% of the 200 shuffled controls on net Sharpe
at least 3 of the 4 variants have net Sharpe at or above the always-held equal-weight benchmark
if_fail: Report it as a failure, with each benchmark's numbers. No extra assets, no re-weighting, no different averages.
if_pass: Still not proof of an edge and not real money. It would be a candidate for a forward test through the signal ledger and then the gate in evidence/gate.json.
